steps.message:
Item 048 on our Package A register falls due on 07/20/2026, and the Block B plant-room excavation the Contractor has planned for 08/10/2026 cannot start until it is closed. I am taking it myself. Item 048 is the Kesterline shoring design for that excavation. Kesterline has since supplemented the sealed Rev.1 with Rev.2, sent under its letter KE-L-2026-0713, which is attached, and is asking for verification on that basis so that the excavation can go ahead. Verify the item on its current revision against the logged groundwater and subsurface conditions.

Work it through against the project record and issue the verification memo, addressed to Rachel Marlbeck, on the attached memorandum form, keeping its sections. Set out the basis you applied, your findings with the working behind them, and the disposition; say which of the design's checks can be carried forward as they stand and which, if any, cannot; say what the excavation this item releases would do to the permanent work already built at Block B; say what has to be produced before the excavation can start and who has to produce it; and say what the disposition means for the 08/10/2026 excavation start. Give the register response you would record under my name, A. Vance, dated 07/20/2026, and the status the item should carry, closing it only if you have verified it. Save the memo as /filesystem/Thelbridge_Verification_Memo_Item048_BlockB.docx.

The Package A site is located at 1802 Larchwood Avenue, on the western portion of the Thornbury State

by an existing campus surface parking lot, to the south by an unimproved landscaped strip and to the west by an

ground westward toward a former off-site low area. The transition between the two elevations is gradual across

present beneath Block B in its current condition.
3.2  Regional and Local Geology
Columbus, Ohio lies within the Till Plains section of the Central Lowland physiographic province. Regional
surficial geology is dominated by Wisconsinan-age glacial deposits — chiefly clay-rich till, glaciolacustrine silt
and clay, and outwash sand and gravel — overlying Devonian-age carbonate and shale bedrock. Local
hydrogeology is characterized by a shallow phreatic surface within the outwash and reworked outwash sands, a
laterally continuous fine-grained aquitard, and a lower confined aquifer within basal outwash sand and gravel
above bedrock.
The subsurface conditions encountered in the Package A borings are consistent with this regional framework: a
medium-dense reworked outwash sand at the surface, a low-permeability clay of glaciolacustrine origin at
intermediate depth, and a dense outwash sand and gravel aquifer at depth. Bedrock was not encountered within
the maximum boring depth of 90 ft (approximately El. 660.0). Blow counts in the SW-GW below El. 720.0
were consistently in the range N ≥ 50 blows per 6 inches, indicating a very dense sand-and-gravel deposit
suitable as a pile-bearing stratum.
3.3  Site History and Prior Use
Site historical review — including review of Franklin County parcel records, USGS topographic maps (1955
and later editions), and Thornbury State University campus master planning archives — indicates that the
Package A parcel was in agricultural use through approximately 1958, was acquired by the University in 1962,
and has been used for surface parking and landscape maintenance since. No prior structures of consequence, no
known below-grade utilities (other than a single abandoned 6-inch clay drain traced along the historic swale in
Block B), and no known industrial fill are present within the footprint. Because there is essentially no prior fill
of engineering significance, the Block B footprint requires new engineered fill — placed on the natural
clay-upper-sand contact after removal of the topsoil mantle — to bring the site to design grade.

THELBRIDGE PROJECT MANAGEMENT SERVICES
500 South High Street, Suite 720, Columbus, OH 43215  |  (614) 555-0125  |  thelbridgepm.com
VERIFICATION MEMORANDUM
To:	Rachel Marlbeck, University Program Director, Thornbury State University
From:	Adrian Vance, Project Engineer (Structural/Geotechnical), Thelbridge Project Management Services
Date:	07/20/2026
1.  PURPOSE
This memorandum addresses Verification Register Item 048 on the Thelbridge Review Comment and Verification Register — Package A. Item 048 is the Kesterline Engineering, PC shoring design (Submittal 31-SH-B) for the Block B plant-room excavation support of excavation (SOE). The item falls due on 07/20/2026. The Block B plant-room excavation planned by the Contractor for 08/10/2026 cannot start until this item is closed.

The purpose of this verification is to determine whether Submittal 31-SH-B Rev.1 (Block B Plant-Room Shoring Calculations, sealed 06/11/2026), as supplemented by the Revision 2 Engineering Supplement (Letter Reference KE-L-2026-0713, dated 07/13/2026, sealed 07/13/2026), is adequate against the logged groundwater and subsurface conditions established in the project record, and whether the excavation this item releases can proceed on the Contractor's planned 08/10/2026 start date.
2.  DOCUMENTS REVIEWED
Submittal 31-SH-B Rev.1: Block B Plant-Room Support of Excavation Design Package — Support of Excavation Design Calculations, Kesterline Engineering, PC, sealed 06/11/2026 (Rev.1).
Submittal 31-SH-B Rev.2 Supplement (KE-L-2026-0713): Revision 2 Engineering Supplement to Submittal 31-SH-B Rev.1, Block B Plant-Room Support of Excavation, Kesterline Engineering, PC, dated 07/13/2026, sealed 07/13/2026.
Geotechnical Investigation Report KGI-2024-0417 Rev.2: Birchwood Village Expansion Program — Package A, Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc., dated 02/14/2025.
Boring Logs and Groundwater Monitoring Records B-01 through B-09: Appendix A to KGI-2024-0417 Rev.2, compiled 06/30/2026, monitoring through 06/28/2026.
Design Basis Memorandum CB-DBM-001 Rev.2: Codes, Loads and Load Combinations — Package A, Calloway Braddock Structural Engineers, LLC, sealed 11/14/2025.
Calculation CB-STR-011 Rev.0: Basement Mat — Global and Local Design, Blocks A and B, Calloway Braddock Structural Engineers, LLC, sealed 12/05/2025.
Thelbridge Review Comment and Verification Register — Package A: Thelbridge_Verification_Register_PkgA.xlsx, Register sheet, Item 048.
Progress Meeting Minutes No. 26: Issued 07/10/2026, Thelbridge Project Management Services.
Pre-Pour Reinforcement and Cover Inspection Sheet: Form TPM-PP-2026-07, dated 07/13/2026.
3.  BASIS OF REVIEW
Governing Specification: Section 31 50 00 — Excavation Support and Protection (delegated design), and Section 31 20 00 Rev.3 — Earthwork and Support of Excavation.
Geotechnical Baseline: Kelbrook Geotechnical Investigation Report KGI-2024-0417 Rev.2 (02/14/2025) and Boring Logs/Groundwater Monitoring (through 06/28/2026). The governing subsurface conditions are: (a) Upper sand (SP-SM) from grade to El. 738.0, γ = 118 pcf, design water table El. 742.0; (b) Compressible clay aquitard (CL) from El. 738.0 to El. 720.0, 18 ft thick, γ = 120 pcf, su = 1,400 psf, c' = 100 psf, φ' = 26°; (c) Dense sand and gravel aquifer (SW-GW) below El. 720.0, γ = 130 pcf, confined piezometric head El. 738.0. The shallow and deep groundwater regimes are confirmed independent across the 19-round monitoring record (11/2024–06/2026).
Design Basis Memorandum: CB-DBM-001 Rev.2 (11/14/2025) establishes design water table El. 742.0 and confined piezometric head El. 738.0 as governing values.
Structural Baseline: Basement mat underside at El. 731.5 (CB-STR-011), top of mat at El. 734.5, 3.0 ft thick. The mat is founded in the SP-SM upper sand above the clay aquitard. The Blocks A/B basement excavation subgrade (El. 731.5) is above the top of clay (El. 738.0) and above the confined head (El. 738.0) but below the shallow water table (El. 742.0).
Verification Register: Item 048, due 07/20/2026, assigned to A. Vance. The register requires written verification before permanent work (Level-3 pour, contractual hold-point 07/22/2026).
Rev.2 Supersession Scope: Per KE-L-2026-0713 Table 1, Rev.2 supersedes Rev.1 Sections 3.4, 4.3, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10. Rev.1 Sections 1, 2, 3.1–3.3, 4.1, 4.2, 8, 11.3, 11.4, 12, 13 remain in force. The verification addresses the combined Rev.1+Rev.2 design as a single integrated submission.
4.  FINDINGS
4.1  Groundwater Conditions and Rev.2 Supersession of the Dry-Excavation Assumption
Rev.1 Section 3.4 assumed a dry excavation from El. 750.0 to El. 726.0 based on the Contractor's Dewatering Plan Submittal 31-DW-A Rev.1. Kesterline Rev.2 (KE-L-2026-0713, Section R2.1) formally withdraws this assumption. The Contractor has confirmed that Submittal 31-DW-A Rev.1 is limited to the Block A basement and does not extend to the Block B plant-room excavation. The Rev.2 design correctly adopts the logged groundwater conditions from KGI-2024-0417 Rev.2 and the monitoring record through 06/28/2026:
• Design phreatic water table behind wall (shallow, upper sand): El. 742.0 (stable range El. 741.6–742.4 across 57 readings).
• Confined piezometric head (deep SW-GW aquifer below El. 720.0): El. 738.0 (stable range El. 737.7–738.3 across 38 readings).
• Clay aquitard (CL) from El. 738.0 to El. 720.0 separates the two regimes; no hydraulic short-circuiting observed.
The Rev.2 design requires four 8-in pressure-relief wells (RW-B1 to RW-B4) screened El. 718.0 to 705.0, actively pumped to hold confined head ≤ El. 726.5. Three vibrating-wire piezometers (VW-B1 to VW-B3, tips at El. 719.0) shall verify depressurization. A mandatory 72-hour confirmation hold is required before excavating below El. 732.0. This approach is consistent with the geotechnical report Section 9.4 recommendation for pressure-relief wells. Finding: The Rev.2 groundwater model matches the logged conditions; the dry-excavation assumption in Rev.1 is correctly superseded.
4.2  Excavation Base Heave Verification (Rev.2 Section R2.2)
Final subgrade El. 726.0 leaves a 6.0 ft clay plug (El. 726.0 to El. 720.0) above the confined aquifer. At the controlled piezometric head El. 726.5, the uplift pressure is u = 6.5 ft × 62.4 pcf = 405.6 psf. The factored resisting plug weight is 0.9W = 0.9 × (6.0 ft × 120 pcf) = 648 psf. Factor of safety FSheave = 648 / 405.6 = 1.60 ≥ 1.50 required per DBM §6.2. Finding: Base heave stability is verified at the controlled head. This check is contingent on the relief wells maintaining the confined head at or below El. 726.5 throughout excavation and until the plant-room slab is cast.
4.3  Layered Effective-Stress plus Hydrostatic Lateral Loading (Rev.2 Section R2.3)
Rev.2 replaces the Rev.1 blended-profile dry case with a layered effective-stress analysis plus full hydrostatic water pressure below El. 742.0. Soil unit weights: fill/upper sand 118 pcf (El. 750–738), clay 120 pcf (El. 738–720), dense sand/gravel 130 pcf (below El. 720). Uniform surcharge 250 psf. The total horizontal driving load above subgrade is 19,610 lb/ft with a driving moment about the anchor (El. 745.5) of 237,293 ft-lb/ft. This comprises 11,623 lb/ft from layered soil+surcharge (moment arm 10.68 ft) and 7,987 lb/ft hydrostatic (moment arm 14.17 ft). The vertical overburden at subgrade is σv0 = 3,106 psf. Finding: The layered analysis is correct and conservative; it properly accounts for the confined aquifer hydrostatic pressure on the wall below El. 742.0, which Rev.1 omitted.
4.4  Sheet-Pile Toe Embedment (Rev.2 Section R2.4)
The sheet-pile tip is lowered from Rev.1 El. 722.0 to Rev.2 El. 719.5 (total length 30.5 ft, embedment D = 6.5 ft below subgrade). The toe extends 0.5 ft into the SW-GW stratum. Undrained analysis in CL clay (su = 1,400 psf): net passive resistance pn = 4su − σv0 = 4(1,400) − 3,106 = 2,494 psf. Over D = 6.5 ft: Pp = 16,211 lb/ft at El. 722.75. Resisting moment about anchor MR = 368,800 ft-lb/ft. FStoe = 368,800 / 237,293 = 1.55 ≥ 1.50. Finding: Toe embedment is adequate with the revised tip at El. 719.5. The sheet piles are not credited as a cutoff against confined aquifer flow; the aquifer is controlled by relief wells. The interlocks are to be sealed over the aquitard interval per Geotechnical Report Section 9.6.
4.5  Tieback Ground Anchor Design (Rev.2 Section R2.5)
Single row at El. 745.5, 20° below horizontal, 6 ft o.c., 25 ft free length + 24 ft bond length. Allowable passive toe resistance Pp,allow = 16,211 / 1.50 = 10,807 lb/ft. Required horizontal anchor reaction Th = 19,610 − 10,807 = 8,803 lb/ft. Design anchor working load Tdesign = (8,803 × 6.0) / cos 20° = 56.2 kips. Ultimate bond capacity Qult = π × 6.0 in × 288 in × 20 psi = 108.6 kips. FSanchor = 108.6 / 56.2 = 1.93. Tendon: (4) 0.6-in Grade 270 strand, design strength 140 kips. Proof test 1.33 × 56.2 = 74.8 kips; lock-off 0.75 × 56.2 = 42.2 kips. Finding: Anchor design is adequate. The reduced anchor load (56.2 kips vs. Rev.1 100 kips) reflects the credited passive toe resistance under the revised loading.
4.6  Sheet-Pile Flexural Check (Rev.2 Section R2.6)
PZ-35 Grade 50 retained (Sx = 48.5 in³/ft). Mallow = 121 kip-ft/ft (Fb = 30 ksi). Under Rev.2 loading, Mmax = 62.4 kip-ft/ft at El. 733.1 (point of zero shear). FSflex = 121 / 62.4 = 1.94 ≥ 1.50. Finding: PZ-35 section is structurally adequate under the revised loading. The flexural demand is lower than Rev.1 (71.2 kip-ft/ft) due to the deeper toe embedment and credited passive resistance.
4.7  Wall Deflection and Instrumentation Triggers (Rev.2 Section R2.7)
Predicted maximum lateral deflection = 1.3 in at El. 738.0. Allowable H/200 = 288/200 = 1.44 in. OK. Mandatory stop-work trigger: if any piezometer (VW-B1 through VW-B3) reads above El. 727.0 during excavation below El. 732.0, excavation ceases until relief-well pumping restores head ≤ El. 726.5. Finding: Deflection estimate is within tolerance; the piezometer trigger provides a direct operational link to the groundwater control requirement.
4.8  Checks Carried Forward from Rev.1 Without Modification
The following Rev.1 sections remain in force per the supersession matrix (KE-L-2026-0713 Table 1):
• Sections 1, 2 — Project scope, codes, site reference documents.
• Sections 3.1–3.3 — Subsurface stratigraphy and soil design parameters (match KGI-2024-0417 Rev.2).
• Sections 4.1, 4.2 — Surface surcharge (250 psf construction) and equipment restriction (10 ft perimeter zone).
• Section 8 — Global overturning and sliding stability checks (FS = 2.06 OK).
• Sections 11.3, 11.4 — Waler, bearing plate, anchor head details (MC 12×50 doubled channels, OK).
• Sections 12, 13 — Construction sequence and monitoring (superseded in part by R2.1 and R2.7 for monitoring triggers).
Finding: These checks can be carried forward as they stand, subject to the Rev.2 modifications to construction sequence (relief-well installation, 72-hour hold, piezometer triggers added to Section 13.1/13.2).
4.9  Checks That CANNOT Be Carried Forward from Rev.1
The following Rev.1 checks are superseded and must be replaced by the Rev.2 calculations:
• Section 3.4 — Dry-excavation assumption (withdrawn; replaced by R2.1 groundwater model).
• Section 4.3 — Dry lateral pressure diagram (replaced by R2.3 layered effective-stress + hydrostatic).
• Section 5 — Excavation base stability (replaced by R2.2 base heave verification).
• Section 6 — Sheet-pile toe embedment at El. 722.0 (replaced by R2.4 at El. 719.5, D = 6.5 ft).
• Section 7 — Tieback anchor design at 100 kips (replaced by R2.5 at 56.2 kips).
• Section 9 — Sheet-pile flexural check at Mmax = 71.2 kip-ft/ft (replaced by R2.6 at Mmax = 62.4 kip-ft/ft).
• Section 10 — Wall deflection at 1.2 in / monitoring without piezometer triggers (replaced by R2.7 at 1.3 in with piezometer stop-work trigger).
Finding: These seven Rev.1 checks are invalidated by the groundwater correction and cannot be used.
4.10  Effect on Permanent Work Already Built at Block B
The Blocks A/B basement mat (underside El. 731.5, top El. 734.5) was cast on 01/12/2026 (per monitoring round 16 notes). The mat is founded in the SP-SM upper sand at El. 731.5, above the top of the clay aquitard (El. 738.0). The plant-room excavation subgrade is El. 726.0, which is 5.5 ft below the mat underside. The excavation is in the southwest quadrant of Block B, east of the shared basement mat. The sheet-pile wall forms a continuous perimeter around the plant-room footprint. The geotechnical report (Section 9.6) requires that any penetration of the clay aquitard be sealed at the aquitard elevation to avoid short-circuiting. The Rev.2 design provides for bentonite-cement grout seals on relief wells (El. 721.0–738.0) and temporary drill casing grouted over the aquitard interval for anchor installation. The sheet-pile interlocks are to be sealed over the aquitard interval. The predicted wall deflection (1.3 in max) and behind-wall settlement (≤ 0.5 in at wall face, zero at ~36 ft) do not reach the basement mat (the mat perimeter is beyond the 1H:1V influence zone from the plant-room excavation, per Rev.1 Section 4.4). Finding: The excavation does not compromise the permanent basement mat already built, provided the aquitard sealing requirements are met and the wall deflection remains within the predicted envelope.
4.11  Prerequisites for Excavation Start
Before excavation can start on 08/10/2026, the following must be produced and verified:
1. Relief-well installation records for RW-B1 through RW-B4 (four 8-in wells, screened El. 718–705, grout seal El. 721–738), by the Contractor's dewatering subcontractor.
2. Piezometer installation records for VW-B1 through VW-B3 (tips at El. 719.0), by the Contractor's instrumentation subcontractor.
3. 72-hour confirmation hold: continuous piezometer readings confirming confined head ≤ El. 726.5 before excavating below El. 732.0, enforced by the Contractor's Superintendent with Owner's Representative witness.
4. Sheet-pile driving records confirming tip elevation El. 719.5 continuously around the perimeter, interlock sealing over the aquitard interval (El. 738–720), by the Contractor's shoring subcontractor.
5. Tieback anchor installation and proof-test records (74.8 kips proof, 42.2 kips lock-off) for all anchors at 6 ft o.c., by the Contractor's anchor subcontractor.
6. Updated site logistics plan enforcing the 10-ft heavy-equipment restriction behind the wall, by the Contractor.
7. Dewatering discharge permit (Ohio EPA NPDES) for relief-well pumping, by the Contractor.
All of the above are Contractor/subcontractor deliverables. The Owner's Representative (Thelbridge) verifies compliance before releasing the excavation hold point.
5.  CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATION
Based on the verification against the logged groundwater and subsurface conditions (KGI-2024-0417 Rev.2, monitoring through 06/28/2026), the Design Basis Memorandum (CB-DBM-001 Rev.2), and the structural baseline (CB-STR-011), Submittal 31-SH-B Rev.1 as supplemented by the Revision 2 Engineering Supplement (KE-L-2026-0713, sealed 07/13/2026) is GEOTECHNICALLY AND STRUCTURALLY ADEQUATE for the Block B plant-room support of excavation, subject to the conditions and prerequisites identified in Findings 4.1 through 4.11 above.

Disposition: VERIFIED WITH CONDITIONS.

The register item 048 is CLOSED as VERIFIED, with the following conditions attached to the closure:
(a) The four relief wells (RW-B1–RW-B4) and three verification piezometers (VW-B1–VW-B3) must be installed and operational before excavation begins.
(b) The 72-hour piezometric confirmation hold at ≤ El. 726.5 is a mandatory hold point before excavating below El. 732.0.
(c) The stop-work trigger at piezometer reading > El. 727.0 during excavation below El. 732.0 must be enforced.
(d) Sheet-pile tip El. 719.5 and interlock sealing over the clay aquitard (El. 738–720) must be achieved.
(e) All anchors must be proof-tested to 74.8 kips and locked off at 42.2 kips.
(f) The 10-ft heavy-equipment restriction behind the wall must be in the site logistics plan and enforced.

Impact on 08/10/2026 excavation start: The verification closes Item 048 on its due date (07/20/2026), removing the register hold on the excavation. The 08/10/2026 start date is achievable provided the Contractor completes the prerequisites in Finding 4.11 (relief wells, piezometers, sheet piling, anchors) in the three-week window from 07/20 to 08/10. The 72-hour confirmation hold adds a minimum 3-day delay after the first lift to El. 732.0, which must be factored into the Contractor's detailed excavation schedule. No further verification action by Thelbridge is required before excavation start, other than witnessing the 72-hour hold and confirming the installation records.
